standard: UK Consumer Rights Act 2015 + Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013

obligations.title: 30-day short-term right to reject faulty goods
obligations.body: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, if goods do not conform to the contract (not of satisfactory quality, not fit for purpose, or not as described), the consumer has a short-term right to reject within 30 days of delivery (or installation) and is entitled to a full refund. The trader may not make any deduction for use during this period.

obligations.title: Repair / replacement / price reduction after 30 days
obligations.body: After the 30-day rejection period, the consumer is entitled to one attempt at repair or replacement. If that fails, or is not possible within a reasonable time without significant inconvenience, the consumer can claim a price reduction (up to 100%) or a final rejection refund. Digital content carries equivalent repair/replacement/price-reduction rights.

obligations.title: 14-day cancellation for distance/online contracts
obligations.body: The Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 give UK consumers a 14-day cancellation right for distance sales (online, by phone, mail order) with no reason required. The trader must provide the cancellation right clearly before contract; failure to do so extends the cancellation period by up to 12 months.

obligations.title: Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill
obligations.body: Under CRA 2015 Part 1 Chapter 4, a service must be carried out with reasonable care and skill, at a reasonable price (if not agreed) and within a reasonable time. If the service falls short, the consumer is entitled to require the trader to repeat the service or to a price reduction, and the trader must not exclude these statutory rights in B2C contracts.
